keywords: someone took money from my account
name: Your bank's fraud line
why: every bank runs a 24-hour fraud line that can block your card and account in minutes, and the first call is what limits the loss
fits: you think money has been taken, your phone lost signal for no reason, you shared an OTP or PIN by mistake, or your card or phone is gone
not_when: nothing has happened yet and you only want to tighten settings; do that inside the app and save the number for later
setup: save your bank's fraud number from the app or the back of your card → if something happens, phone it from any phone → ask for the card and account to be blocked and a fraud case opened → open a SAPS case → register with SAFPS
walkthrough: Save the number now, before anything happens, from the back of your card or inside the banking app, never from an SMS: Capitec 0860 10 20 43, FNB 087 575 9444, Standard Bank 0800 222 050, Absa 0860 557 557, Nedbank 0800 110 929, GoTyme (TymeBank) 0860 999 119.

If your phone suddenly has no signal, treat it as a SIM swap: phone your network from another phone to stop the swap, then phone the bank's fraud line and ask them to block the account and the banking profile.
If someone phoned 'from the bank' and you gave an OTP, PIN or approved an app message, hang up and phone the fraud line yourself immediately; do not wait to see if money moves.
Tell the agent exactly what happened and ask for three things: block the card, block the account or app profile, and open a fraud case with a reference number; write the reference down.
Go to the nearest police station and open a case the same day with that reference; the bank's investigation and any insurance will ask for the SAPS case number.
Register with SAFPS for free Protective Registration on safps.org.za so nobody can open credit in your name, and pull your free credit report a month later to check.
Never give your PIN, password or OTP to the person who phones you, even if they know your name and ID number; the real bank's fraud desk never asks for them.
ten_minute_action: Open your banking app, find the fraud or 'report fraud' number, and save it in your phone as 'Bank fraud line' right now, then switch on transaction notifications in the app.
cost: free: fraud lines are toll-free or standard-rate and blocking a card costs nothing (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Council for Debt Collectors register and complaints
why: every debt collector must be registered with the Council; the register tells you in a minute whether the person phoning you is allowed to, and the Council disciplines the ones who break the rules, free
fits: a collector or agency is contacting you and you want to check they are real, or they have threatened you, phoned your employer or added fees
not_when: the person is the original lender or their attorney acting under a court order; those complaints go to the NCR, the ombud or the court
setup: ask the collector for their registration number → check it on cfdc.org.za or by phone → keep a log of every call → if rules are broken, write a sworn complaint → send it to the Council
walkthrough: Ask the caller for their full name, the company, and their Council for Debt Collectors registration number; a registered collector has one and will give it.

Check it on the Council's website at cfdc.org.za or phone the Council on 012 804 9808 and ask whether that name and company are registered; an unregistered collector is committing a criminal offence and you need not deal with them.
Start a log in your notes app: date, time, name, what was said; it becomes the evidence if they threaten you, phone your family or employer, or pretend to be a sheriff.
Ask in writing for a full statement of the debt showing the original amount, payments, interest and every fee; collector fees are limited to the regulated tariff.
If a rule is broken, write a complaint as an affidavit: what happened, when, who, what you want done; sign it in front of a commissioner of oaths (any police station does this free).
Send it to the Council by email to info@cfdc.org.za or through the complaint form on cfdc.org.za, with your call log and any SMSes attached; the Council notifies the collector and investigates.
Never pay cash to a collector at your door and never give card details over the phone; pay only into the account on the written statement, and only what you agreed in writing.
ten_minute_action: Message the collector who last contacted you: 'Please send me your Council for Debt Collectors registration number and a written statement of the account.' Then check the number on cfdc.org.za.
cost: free: checking the register and lodging a complaint cost nothing (Council for Debt Collectors FAQ, checked 2026-10-30)

name: DebiCheck and debit order control in your banking app
why: a DebiCheck mandate is a debit order you approved in your own app, so nothing new can be collected without you, and the same screen lets you dispute and reverse one that is wrong
fits: you have debit orders for debts, policies or accounts and want them timed for payday and nothing unexpected going off
not_when: you have no bank account; cash payments are controlled by the envelope, not the app
setup: open the debit orders screen in your banking app → list every mandate → move each date to the day after money lands → approve only mandates you recognise → dispute any wrong debit within 60 days
walkthrough: Open your banking app and find 'Debit orders' or 'DebiCheck' (Capitec: Transact, Debit orders; FNB: My Bank Accounts, Debit orders; Standard Bank: Transact, Debit orders; Absa, Nedbank and GoTyme have the same under the account menu).
Write every debit order on your month plan: company, amount, date. Anything you do not recognise goes on a dispute list.
Phone each company and move its date to the day after your money lands; most change it on the call, and a debit order that lands before payday is the one that bounces and costs a declined fee.

When a DebiCheck approval request arrives by SMS or in the app, check the company, the amount and the date against your list before you tap Approve; decline anything unknown, and a lender cannot collect without the approval.

For a debit you never agreed to, open it in the app and choose Dispute (FNB and Absa let you dispute in-app; amounts over R200 at some banks need the call centre); from 13 April 2026 the window is 60 calendar days after the debit.

Phone the company the same day and cancel the agreement in writing, or the debit returns next month; a disputed DebiCheck that matched what you approved will usually not be reversed, so approve carefully.
If the company keeps debiting, lodge a free complaint with the National Financial Ombud on 0860 800 900; never close the account to escape a debit order, the debt follows you.
ten_minute_action: Open your banking app, go to Debit orders, and write down every one with its date; circle any that go off before your payday and phone that company tomorrow to move it.
cost: free to approve, move and dispute debit orders; a declined debit order costs a fee set by your bank (GoTyme publishes R3; check yours) and the dispute window is 60 days from 13 April 2026 (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Experian free credit report (Up platform)
why: Experian is one of the big registered bureaus and gives your report free through its Up platform, with disputes logged on the same site, and its WhatsApp line for consumer queries
fits: you want to see what lenders see and dispute what is wrong, on your phone, with no payment
not_when: you have never had any account, loan or contract; the bureau may hold no file on you yet
setup: go to up.experian.co.za → register with your own ID details → verify by OTP → view and download the report → dispute wrong items on the same platform
walkthrough: On your phone open up.experian.co.za (Up, Powered by Experian); registration is free and you will be asked for your South African ID number on their site, not anywhere else.
Create a login with your email and cellphone number and confirm the OTP they send.
Open your credit report and read the accounts list first: mark any account you do not recognise, any account with no payment for 3 years, and anything paid that still shows as owing.
Download or screenshot the report and keep it in a folder on your phone with the date; you will compare it in 3 months.

To dispute an item, use the dispute option on the same platform: name the account, say what is wrong, attach your paid-up letter or statement; Experian must investigate free within 20 business days under section 72 of the National Credit Act.
If the site cannot verify you, message Experian's consumer WhatsApp on +27 79 127 4906 or use the contact page on experian.co.za.
Never use a lookalike site that asks for a card to 'release' your free report; the free report under the National Credit Act never needs a card.
ten_minute_action: Open up.experian.co.za on your phone, register with your email and cellphone number, and open your report; mark anything you do not recognise.
cost: free: Experian provides free access to your report through Up, and the NCA guarantees one free report a year from each bureau (checked 2026-10-30)

name: FSCA licence check
why: anyone selling investments, insurance or financial advice must be licensed by the FSCA; the register tells you in two minutes whether the name and the FSP number match, and scammers borrow real numbers
fits: someone is offering you an investment, trading group, funeral policy or 'advisor' service and you want to know if it is real before any money moves
not_when: the money is going to your own bank's savings product inside its app; the bank is already licensed
setup: ask for the registered name and FSP number → search the FSCA register on fsca.co.za or phone 0800 110 443 → check the name matches the number and the licence covers that product → check the licence is current
walkthrough: Ask the person or company, in writing, for their registered name, their FSP number and the name of the individual's own licence; a real provider sends it without fuss.
Go to fsca.co.za on your phone and find the 'FSP search' (also reachable at fsca.co.za/Fais/Search_FSP.htm) and search by the FSP number.

Check 3 things on the result: the name on the register is the same as the name you were given, the licence status is active, and the categories cover the product you are being sold (a short-term insurance licence does not cover investments).
If you cannot use the site, phone the FSCA on 0800 110 443 and ask them to confirm the name and number; it is free.
If the number is not found, belongs to another company, or the licence has lapsed, stop: do not send money, and keep the messages as evidence.
Report a fake or borrowed licence to the FSCA by phone or on their site, and warn the person who introduced you.
Never accept 'we are exempt from licensing' or 'registered with CIPC' as proof; a CIPC company number is not a financial services licence.
ten_minute_action: Message the person offering you the investment: 'Please send me your FSP number and registered company name.' Then search the number on fsca.co.za before you reply.
cost: free: the FSCA register and the 0800 110 443 line cost nothing (checked 2026-10-30)

name: GoTyme Bank EveryDay account
why: a transactional account with no monthly fee, opened in the app in minutes with cash in and out at Pick n Pay and Boxer tills, so moving your own money stops costing you
fits: you pay a monthly account fee or ATM fees now, or you have no bank account and want one that costs nothing to hold
not_when: you need a branch to walk into for every query; GoTyme is app, kiosk and phone, not branches
setup: download the GoTyme Bank app → open the account with your ID → collect or activate your card at a Pick n Pay or Boxer kiosk → move your debit orders and income → check the fee page in the app
walkthrough: Download the GoTyme Bank app from the official app store (the bank was TymeBank until January 2026; existing TymeBank customers were moved over and the old app is being retired) and open an account with your ID; the bank says it takes under five minutes.

Read the fees screen in the app before you use it: GoTyme's published fee page lists a free current account with no monthly charge, free card purchases, and small fees for some things, such as R3 for a declined debit order and a fee for a SendMoney voucher to someone without a GoTyme account; the app is the source, so confirm there.
Get your card at a Pick n Pay or Boxer kiosk, and use the supermarket till for cash withdrawals and deposits rather than an ATM; ask the kiosk what the till fee is, since the published pages differ.
Move your income to the account: give your employer or SASSA the new account details (SASSA changes bank details at its office, not by phone), and move your debit orders to the day after money lands.
Use PayShap or SendMoney inside the app for payments to people; GoTyme was reported to charge R0 for PayShap, confirm in the app.
Download a statement from the app at the end of the month and add up every fee line; the number should be close to zero.
Never give your app PIN or an OTP to anyone who phones, and save GoTyme's fraud line 0860 999 119 from the app.
ten_minute_action: Download the GoTyme Bank app, start the account opening with your ID beside you, and read the fees screen before you finish so you know what every action costs.
cost: R0 monthly fee on GoTyme's published fee page; small per-use fees for some actions (for example R3 for a declined debit order); published figures differ for till cash and SendMoney, so confirm in the GoTyme app (checked 2026-10-30)

name: GoTyme GoalSave
why: a free savings pocket inside the GoTyme app, separate from the everyday money, with interest from day one and a 10-day notice option that is exactly the speed bump a cushion needs
fits: you bank with GoTyme and want the cushion or a goal kept apart from spending money, growing by itself on payday
not_when: you bank elsewhere; your own bank's savings pocket does the same job, the separation is what matters
setup: open the GoTyme app → tap Save, then GoalSave → name it and set the target → move the first amount today → set a recurring transfer for the day after payday
walkthrough: Open the GoTyme Bank app, tap 'Save' and choose 'GoalSave'; opening one is free and you can have several (GoTyme's page says up to 20, with a combined cap of R250,000).
Name it for its job, 'Cushion' or 'School fees', and type the target number from your plan; the name is what stops you spending it.

Read the interest terms on the screen at that moment: GoTyme's GoalSave page describes 6% a year from day one and up to 10% a year if you give 10 days' notice before closing, while other published descriptions differ, so the app is the source.
Move the first amount today from your EveryDay account, even R20, so the pocket exists before payday.
Set a recurring transfer to the GoalSave for the day after your money lands, for the amount in pot 2 of your month plan.
When you need the money, choose the notice option if you can wait 10 days to earn the full interest; immediate withdrawal is allowed but may pay less.
Never borrow to put money into a GoalSave; no savings rate beats the interest on a loan.
ten_minute_action: Open the GoTyme app, tap Save, open a GoalSave called 'Cushion', and move R20 into it right now so it exists before payday.
cost: free to open; GoTyme's own GoalSave page describes 6% a year rising to 10% a year with 10 days' notice, up to 20 GoalSaves and R250,000 combined; published tiers differ, so confirm in the GoTyme app (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Municipal indigent office
why: the municipality's own office is the only place that can put your household on the indigent register, and that register is what unlocks free basic electricity, water and rates relief every month
fits: household income is low, someone gets a grant or pension, and you pay for electricity, water or rates
not_when: your household income is clearly above your municipality's published limit; ask anyway if you are not sure, the limits differ widely
setup: find your municipality's customer care or indigent office → ask for the indigent application form and the income limit → bring ID, proof of income, a municipal statement or prepaid token and bank statements → apply → claim the free token every month
walkthrough: Find your municipality's customer care centre or indigent office (the address is on your municipal statement, on the municipality's website, or ask at the ward councillor's office).

Ask for the 'indigent register' or 'free basic services' application form and the current income limit; it is set by your municipality (Ekurhuleni published about R10,479 a month in 2026, many smaller towns far less).

Take your ID, proof of income or an affidavit that you have none (the office or a police station commissions it free), your latest municipal statement or a prepaid electricity token, and 3 months of bank statements if you have an account.
If the property is not in your name, bring a letter or affidavit from the owner saying you live there.
Hand in the form and ask for a receipt with the date; approval can take a few months, so ask when to come back.

Once approved, ask how to claim the free electricity: Eskom-supplied households dial *130*269# on the first of each month, municipal customers get it where they buy electricity; the free units do not carry over.
Diary the renewal date; most registers lapse after a year if you do not reapply, and never pay anyone to 'fast-track' the application.
ten_minute_action: Find your municipality's customer care number on your last municipal statement or its website and phone to ask for the indigent income limit and the documents they want.
cost: free to apply; usually 50 kWh of electricity a month (up to 60 kWh in some municipalities) and a water allowance; the income limit is set by each municipality (checked 2026-10-30)

name: NASASA (National Stokvel Association of South Africa)
why: NASASA is the self-regulatory body for stokvels under a Banks Act exemption; it has a sample constitution, registers groups, and takes reports about fake ones, which is the fastest way to tell a stokvel from a scheme
fits: you belong to or run a stokvel, burial society or savings club and want written rules, registration, or to check a group you have been invited to
not_when: the 'stokvel' promises returns or pays for recruiting; that is a pyramid scheme and the report goes to the National Consumer Commission, not NASASA
setup: get the sample constitution from NASASA → adopt it at a meeting → open a bank account in the stokvel's name with 2 or 3 signatures → apply to register by email → show the books at every meeting
walkthrough: Phone NASASA on 010 007 2129 or email info@nasasa.co.za and ask for the sample constitution and the registration form; sources differ on whether registration is required below R100,000 in contributions, so ask them.

At the next meeting, go through the constitution and fill in your group's own rules: members, contribution and date, how and when payouts happen, what happens when someone leaves or dies, and who signs for the money.
Open a bank account in the stokvel's name needing 2 or 3 signatures (most banks have a stokvel account); money never sits in the treasurer's personal account or in cash.
Email the completed form and constitution to info@nasasa.co.za and keep the reply; ask whether there is a fee, since older sources say there is none.
Show the bank statement and the contributions book at every meeting, and give every member a signed receipt line for every contribution.
If you have been invited to a group and want to check it, ask NASASA whether it is registered, and read the constitution yourself before paying anything.
Never hand a bank card or PIN to the treasurer and never pay a contribution without a receipt in the book.
ten_minute_action: Email info@nasasa.co.za and ask for the sample stokvel constitution and the registration form, then read your own group's rules against it.
cost: free to contact; older sources say NASASA membership has no fee, confirm with NASASA on 010 007 2129 (checked 2026-10-30)

name: National Credit Regulator complaints line
why: the NCR is the regulator for every lender and debt counsellor; it is free, it checks registration numbers, and it acts on unregistered lenders, overcharging and reckless credit
fits: a lender or debt counsellor has overcharged you, lent recklessly, is unregistered, or is holding your card or ID
not_when: the complaint is about a bank account, an insurer or a bureau that will not fix a listing; those go to the National Financial Ombud
setup: first raise it with the lender in writing → gather the agreement, statements and messages → phone 0860 627 627 or email complaints@ncr.org.za → fill in form 29 → keep the reference
walkthrough: Write to the lender or counsellor first: what is wrong, what you want, and a date; the NCR asks whether you tried, and the letter becomes evidence.
Gather the papers: the credit agreement, statements, proof of payments, and every SMS or WhatsApp; take photos with your phone if you have only paper.
Phone the NCR on 0860 627 627 (Monday to Thursday 8am to 5pm, Friday to 4:30pm) to check a lender's or counsellor's registration and to ask how to lodge; or email complaints@ncr.org.za.

Download the complaint initiation form (form 29) from ncr.org.za, fill it in with plain facts and dates, and send it with the papers; if someone lodges for you, they need your signed consent form too.
For an unregistered lender (mashonisa) say so clearly: no NCRCP number, the amount lent, what you have paid, and whether they hold your card or ID; the NCR investigates unregistered lending.
Write the reference number down and follow up by phone after 20 business days if you have heard nothing.

Never pay anyone to lodge a complaint for you, and be careful of emails or SMSes claiming to be from the NCR; the NCR has warned of a cyber-attack on its systems, so confirm contact details on ncr.org.za.
ten_minute_action: Phone 0860 627 627 and ask whether the lender or counsellor you are dealing with is registered; give the name and ask for the registration number.
cost: free: the complaint line, the register check and form 29 cost nothing (NCR, checked 2026-10-30)

name: NCR register of debt counsellors
why: only a debt counsellor registered with the NCR can put you under debt review, and the public register is the one way to tell a real counsellor from a removal scam before you sign Form 16
fits: your repayments are more than your income can carry and you are ready to find out about debt review from someone registered
not_when: you can cover every minimum from your income; the snowball clears it without fees or a listing
setup: search the NCR register on ncr.org.za for a counsellor near you → check the NCRDC number and name match → ask the first-call questions → get the fees in writing → sign Form 16 only then
walkthrough: Go to ncr.org.za and open the register of registrants; search for debt counsellors in your province and write down 2 or 3 names with their NCRDC numbers, or phone 0860 627 627 and ask for registered counsellors near you.

Before any meeting, check that the name and the NCRDC number match on the register and the status is active; the NCR's Circular 1 of 2024 warns that unregistered people borrow real counsellors' numbers.

Make the first call and ask 3 questions: what are your fees in rand (application R50 plus a restructuring fee the NCR caps, published figures differ, so ask), which registered payment distribution agent do you use, and how long until the court order.
Ask for the fee quote and the process in writing before you sign Form 16, the application; a real counsellor sends it.
Bring your owed list, your payslips or income proof, your bank statements and your month plan; the counsellor must assess whether you are over-indebted within 30 business days.
Once you sign Form 16, the counsellor sends Form 17.1 to every creditor within 5 business days and your payments go through the distribution agent, not into the counsellor's own account.

Never pay an upfront 'consultation' fee beyond the R50 application, never sign with someone who contacted you first on WhatsApp, and never take new credit once under review; the law does not allow it.
ten_minute_action: Phone the NCR on 0860 627 627 and ask for the names and NCRDC numbers of two registered debt counsellors near you; write them down before you speak to anyone else.
cost: free to search; debt review itself costs an application fee of R50 plus a restructuring fee capped by the NCR (published figures differ, R8,000 to R9,000) and a monthly aftercare fee of 5% with a cap; confirm on ncr.org.za (checked 2026-10-30)

name: National Financial Ombud (NFO)
why: since 1 March 2024 one free ombud handles complaints about banks, lenders, credit bureaus and insurers; it can order refunds, and you do not need a lawyer
fits: your bank, lender, insurer or a credit bureau has treated you unfairly, rejected a valid claim, or will not fix a wrong listing, and you have complained to them first
not_when: you have not yet complained to the company itself; the NFO expects you to give them about 20 working days first
setup: complain to the company in writing and keep the reference → wait up to 20 working days → lodge with the NFO online, by email, WhatsApp or phone → send your evidence → follow the case number
walkthrough: Complain to the bank, lender, insurer or bureau first, in writing, and keep the reference number; the NFO will ask for it and gives the company about 20 working days to respond.
Gather the evidence: statements, the policy or agreement, your complaint and their reply, and any SMS or WhatsApp; photograph paper documents.
Lodge with the NFO: the online form on nfosa.co.za, email info@nfosa.co.za, WhatsApp 076 574 8055 (the number on the NFO's own site; older bank pages show a different one), or phone 0860 800 900.
Write the complaint in plain words: what happened, the dates, what you lost, what you want (a refund, a listing removed, a claim paid), and attach the evidence.
Write down the NFO case number and reply to any request for more information within the time they give.
The NFO's decision can be in your favour and the company must act on it; in its first year it reported more than R400 million returned to consumers.
Never pay a 'claims consultant' to lodge for you; the NFO is free and will deal with you directly.
ten_minute_action: Find the reference number from your complaint to the company, then open nfosa.co.za on your phone and start the online complaint form with it.
cost: free: the National Financial Ombud charges consumers nothing (checked 2026-10-30)

name: NHFC First Home Finance portal
why: the National Housing Finance Corporation runs the First Home Finance subsidy online; its calculator gives your own subsidy number and the portal is the only place to apply without a middleman
fits: a first-time buyer, citizen or permanent resident, with household income of R3,501 to R22,000 a month and a clean enough record to get a home loan
not_when: household income is outside R3,501 to R22,000 a month, you have owned property before, or you already received a housing subsidy
setup: use the calculator on nhfc.co.za → clean the credit record → get a home loan quote and tell the bank you will apply → apply on the portal while a window is open → upload the documents and follow the status
walkthrough: Open nhfc.co.za on your phone, find First Home Finance and run the subsidy calculator with your gross household income; published 2026 figures differ (a top of R169,264 and a bottom of R27,960 or R38,878), so the calculator is your number.
Pull your free credit report and fix what is wrong; a home loan needs months of on-time payments, so start there.
Speak to a bank about a home loan and tell them you will apply for First Home Finance; some banks still want an approval in principle before the subsidy application.
Check nhfc.co.za for whether the application portal is open: the NHFC closes it between windows and says applications outside a window are not accepted.

Register on the First Home Finance online portal and upload what it asks for: ID, proof of income (payslips, or bank statements if you are self-employed), the loan quote, and the consent for NHFC to verify your income with your employer.
Follow the status updates the portal sends at each stage and reply to any request within the time given.
Never pay anyone to submit for you; the NHFC rejects manual submissions by third parties, and never sign an offer to purchase until the subsidy and the loan are both confirmed in writing.
ten_minute_action: Open nhfc.co.za, find the First Home Finance calculator and type in your household's monthly income to see the subsidy amount you could qualify for.
cost: free to apply; the subsidy covers household incomes of R3,501 to R22,000 a month, with published 2026 amounts up to R169,264 (figures differ, use the NHFC calculator) (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Your phone's notes app as a money log
why: the notes app already on your phone is the only tool that works at a taxi rank, with no data, in 10 seconds; a week of lines in it shows more than any budgeting app
fits: you want to see where the money goes, keep your owed list and policy list, and do it on a prepaid phone with no data
not_when: you already keep a full record in a spreadsheet or the bank app and it works for you
setup: open the notes app → make one page per list (Week 1, Owed, Policies, Waiting) → write one line per spend the same day → add up on day 7 → keep the lists where you see them on payday
walkthrough: Open the notes app that is already on your phone (Samsung Notes, Google Keep, Apple Notes) and make a page called 'Week 1' with today's date.
Each time money leaves your hands, write one line the same day: 'taxi R18', 'airtime R12', 'bread R19'; include cash, the small things and money given to a child.
On day 7, add it up, write the total at the bottom, and circle the 3 biggest lines; those are where your month plan starts.
Make a second page called 'Owed': one line per debt with who, how much is left, what you pay a month and the interest or fee; put the most expensive at the top.
Make a third page called 'Policies': each funeral policy or society with the premium, the payout, who is covered and the waiting period.
Make a fourth called 'Waiting' for anything unplanned you want to buy; it waits there 24 hours before any money moves.
Pin the pages or put them in a folder called 'Money', and never store a PIN, password or card number in a note; the notes app is not a safe.
ten_minute_action: Open your phone's notes app, make a page called 'Week 1' with today's date, and write down everything you have spent today, one line each.
cost: free

name: PayShap
why: instant payments to a cellphone number through your own banking app, free or near-free below R100 at most banks, which is where family money and small bills live
fits: you send money to people, pay a stokvel or a share of groceries, and want it instant and cheap without a voucher or a branch
not_when: the person has no bank account at all; a cash voucher or the till is the only route then
setup: open your banking app → find PayShap → register your ShapID (your cellphone number) → ask the person for theirs → send a R10 test → move your small regular payments to it
walkthrough: Open your banking app and find 'PayShap' or 'Pay by cellphone number' (Capitec: Transact, PayShap; FNB: Pay, PayShap; Standard Bank, Absa, Nedbank and GoTyme under Pay or Transfers).
Register your ShapID: your cellphone number linked to this account, so people can pay you by number; it is free.

Look up the PayShap fee in your bank's fee guide in the app: many banks charge R0 under R100 (TymeBank/GoTyme was reported free at every amount; Absa and Standard Bank charge more above R100), and the per-payment limit is R3,000 at some banks and higher at others.
Ask the person you pay to register their ShapID too; at Absa and Nedbank a payment to a ShapID is cheaper than one to an account number.
Send R10 as a test and confirm it arrived instantly; then move your fixed family amount, stokvel contribution and other small payments to PayShap in amounts under R100 where the free rule applies.
Use 'Request money' where your bank has it to be paid back by family or for a shared cost; it is cheaper than chasing cash.
Never pay a stranger by PayShap for something you have not received; it is instant and cannot be reversed, which is why scammers ask for it.
ten_minute_action: Open your banking app, find PayShap, register your cellphone number as your ShapID, and send R10 to a family member to see it land.
cost: free at some banks and mostly free or near-free under R100, up to about R7.50 a payment at others; fees are set by each bank and change, so confirm in your bank's fee guide (checked 2026-10-30)

keywords: someone opened an account in my name
name: SAFPS Protective Registration
why: a free marker against your identity on the fraud-prevention database that every member bank and lender checks, so a credit application in your name triggers a check that it is really you
fits: your ID, passport or phone is lost or stolen, an account was opened in your name, or you sent your ID copy to someone you now distrust
not_when: nothing has been lost or stolen and your credit report is clean; still free, but pull the report first
setup: get a SAPS case number → apply on safps.org.za, by email or by phone → send a certified ID copy with the form → get the reference within 48 hours → dispute any accounts that are not yours
walkthrough: Report the lost or stolen ID, or the account you did not open, at the police station and get the case number; SAFPS and the banks ask for it.

Go to safps.org.za, open 'Apply for Protective Registration' and fill in the form; or email the completed form with a certified copy of your ID to protection@safps.org.za; or phone SAFPS on 011 867 2234.
Get an ID copy certified free at any police station; some guides also ask for proof of address, so take one along.
SAFPS issues a Protective Registration reference number within about 48 hours; save it with your case number.
If a lender already opened credit in your name, ask them in writing for a letter confirming the impersonation; with it, SAFPS can also list you as a victim of impersonation.
Pull your free credit report from each bureau and dispute every account that is not yours, quoting the SAPS case number and the SAFPS reference.
Never post a photo of your ID in a WhatsApp group and never send a copy to a 'job agent' or a 'loan agent'; a copy is all a fraudster needs.
ten_minute_action: Open safps.org.za on your phone, find 'Apply for Protective Registration', and start the form with your ID beside you; it is free.
cost: free: Protective Registration costs nothing and the reference number is issued within about 48 hours (SAFPS, checked 2026-10-30)

name: Open a case at SAPS
why: a police case number is what a bank, an insurer, SAFPS and the NCR all ask for, and it is the record that turns a mashonisa's threat or a stolen card into something the law can act on
fits: someone is threatening you, holding your card or ID, has stolen from you, or has used your identity
not_when: the problem is a civil debt with no threat or crime; that goes to the NCR, the ombud or a debt counsellor
setup: go to the nearest police station (any one, not only your area) → give a statement → get the CAS number → keep it with your other references → ask for the investigating officer's name
walkthrough: Go to the nearest police station; any station must open the case even if the crime happened in another area, and for an emergency phone 10111.
Tell the officer at the desk you want to open a case and give a statement; bring your ID, any messages or screenshots, and for a stolen card the bank's fraud reference.
Give the facts in order with dates and names; the officer writes it as a statement you sign, so read it before you sign.
Ask for the CAS (case) number before you leave and write it down; without it there is no case.
Ask for the name of the investigating officer and the station's number so you can follow up the next working day.
If the desk refuses to open a case, ask calmly for the shift commander, or phone the SAPS National Complaints line on 0800 333 177; nobody may be refused a case.
Give the CAS number to your bank, SAFPS and the NCR; and never pay anyone at the station or anyone who offers to 'make the docket move'.
ten_minute_action: Put your ID, your phone with the screenshots, and the bank's fraud reference in one place, and look up the address of the nearest police station; go today, not tomorrow.
cost: free: opening a case, a statement and a certified copy at a police station cost nothing (checked 2026-10-30)

name: SARS eFiling and the SARS MobiApp
why: the only place a tax refund is claimed; if your employer deducted PAYE and you earned near or under the threshold, or paid medical aid, the refund sits at SARS until you check the auto-assessment or file
fits: you have an IRP5 with PAYE deducted, paid medical aid or retirement contributions, or got an auto-assessment SMS from SARS
not_when: your only income is a grant or cash piece jobs with no tax ever deducted; there is nothing to refund
setup: register on sars.gov.za or in the SARS MobiApp with your ID → check the auto-assessment against your IRP5 → accept by doing nothing if correct, or file the ITR12 if not → confirm your bank account on your profile → wait for the refund
walkthrough: Download the SARS MobiApp from the official app store, or go to sars.gov.za and choose eFiling; register with your ID number and cellphone; if you have no tax number, registration creates one.
Get your IRP5 from your employer (or find it already loaded on your SARS profile) and your medical aid tax certificate if you have one.

In filing season (for the 2026 year, auto-assessments were issued from 1 to 12 July and individual filing ran from 13 July to 23 October 2026), open your assessment in the app and compare the income and deductions with your IRP5.
If it is correct, you do nothing; the refund is paid into the bank account on your SARS profile. If it is wrong, open the ITR12 return in the app, fix it and file before the deadline SARS publishes.
Check that the bank account on your profile is in your own name and verified; SARS pays refunds only to a verified account.
If you are stuck, phone the SARS Contact Centre on 0800 00 7277 or book a branch visit through the app rather than queueing.
Never respond to an SMS or email 'from SARS' with a link to claim a refund; SARS pays refunds through eFiling, and never pay a 'refund agent' who found you on WhatsApp.
ten_minute_action: Download the SARS MobiApp, register with your ID number and cellphone, and look for an auto-assessment or your IRP5 on your profile.
cost: free to register and file; the tax threshold was R95,750 for under-65s for the year to 28 February 2026, and the 2026 individual filing deadline was 23 October 2026 (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Your nearest SASSA office
why: the office is where a permanent grant is applied for, where bank details are changed, and where an unlawful deduction is reported; it is free and the receipt it gives you is proof of the date you applied
fits: someone in your household may qualify for an older person's, child support, disability or foster child grant, or a grant has stopped or is short
not_when: your only question is the R370 SRD grant, which is applied for and checked online only
setup: phone 0800 60 10 11 for the nearest office and the documents → gather ID, birth certificates, proof of income and bank statements → apply in person → keep the receipt → follow up after the decision time
walkthrough: Phone SASSA's toll-free line 0800 60 10 11 and ask for the nearest office, its hours, and the exact documents for the grant you want; offices differ in what they ask.

Gather the usual papers: your 13-digit ID (or the affidavit SASSA accepts if you have none), the child's birth certificate for a child grant, proof of income or an affidavit of no income, proof of marital status, and 3 months of bank statements if you have an account.
For a disability grant, ask the office about the medical assessment; it is done through SASSA's doctor and you do not pay for it.
Go early, apply in person, and make sure you leave with the receipt showing the date; if approved, the grant is paid from that date.
Ask when the decision is due and how you will be told; if it is refused, you have the right to appeal in writing, and the office will tell you the form and the time limit.

To change bank details or report a deduction you did not agree to, go to the office with your ID and the statement; deductions can also be disputed by SMS to 34548 with your ID number and the company's name.
Never pay anyone to help you apply or to 'speed up' a grant; applying is free and SASSA staff may not ask for money.
ten_minute_action: Phone 0800 60 10 11, ask for your nearest SASSA office and the documents needed for the grant someone in your house may qualify for, and write them down.
cost: free to apply; grant amounts reported for April 2026 are R2,400 (older person), R2,420 from age 75 and R580 per child (child support), from news reports, confirm at the office (checked 2026-10-30)

name: SASSA SRD online portal (srd.sassa.gov.za)
why: the R370 grant is applied for, checked and appealed only on this site; it takes a few minutes on a phone and costs nothing
fits: you are 18 to 59, get no other grant or UIF, have little or no income, and have a cellphone number in your name
not_when: you receive another SASSA grant or UIF, or your income is above the threshold SASSA publishes on the site
setup: open srd.sassa.gov.za → apply with your ID number and cellphone number → add banking details in your own name → check status monthly → appeal on the site if declined
walkthrough: Open srd.sassa.gov.za on your phone (the only official site; it extends the grant to 31 March 2027) and choose 'Apply'.
Enter your ID number and a cellphone number registered in your name; SASSA sends OTPs to it, so keep it active.
Add banking details for an account in your own name if you have one; it speeds payment, and you can change them only on this site, never by WhatsApp or phone.
Each month, go to 'Check status' with your ID and cellphone number; SASSA re-checks income every month against bank inflows, so a month can be declined after an earlier approval.
If declined, read the reason shown and appeal on the site within the time it shows, attaching proof if the reason is wrong.
For general questions, phone SASSA's toll-free line 0800 60 10 11; SASSA's WhatsApp line is widely published as 082 046 8553, but confirm it on sassa.gov.za before you trust any number sent to you.
Never pay anyone to apply, 'unlock' or 'fix' your SRD, and never share your ID number or banking details in a WhatsApp group; the real site asks for nothing but what is above.
ten_minute_action: Open srd.sassa.gov.za on your phone, choose Apply or Check status, and enter your ID number and the cellphone number in your name.
cost: free to apply; the grant is R370 a month to 31 March 2027; the income threshold published by third parties is R624 a month, confirm on srd.sassa.gov.za (checked 2026-10-30)

name: A Google Sheets month plan
why: a free sheet on your phone adds up the three pots for you, so on payday you see in one screen whether the month fits before anything is spent
fits: you have a smartphone with some data, income lands once or twice a month, and the notes-app log has shown you where the money goes
not_when: you have no data or your phone struggles with apps; the notes app or a notebook does the same job by hand
setup: install Google Sheets → make a sheet with 3 sections (Bills, Aside, The rest) → type the amounts from your month plan → add the totals → open it on payday and fill in what landed
walkthrough: Install Google Sheets from the official app store (free with a Google account) and create a new sheet called 'Month plan'.

In row 1 type the money that lands on payday (after deductions, lowest month if it changes); in the rows below make three blocks with a heading each: 'Bills' (rent, electricity, every debt minimum, each with its due day), 'Aside' (cushion transfer, family amount), and 'The rest'.
Under each block type the amounts in one column, and at the bottom of each block put a sum formula: =SUM() over that block's amounts.
At the bottom put the calculation that matters: money in, minus Bills, minus Aside; what is left is 'The rest', and divide it by the weeks to the next payday for a weekly food-and-transport number.
On payday, open the sheet, type what actually landed, and pay Bills and move Aside the same day; if the bottom number is negative, that is a debt problem, and the owed list comes first.
After 2 weeks, compare the sheet with your notes-app log and fix the lines that did not fit.
Never keep account numbers, PINs or passwords in the sheet; amounts and names only.
ten_minute_action: Install Google Sheets, make a sheet called 'Month plan', and type the three headings Bills, Aside and The rest with the amounts from your notes-app log.
cost: free

name: A tax-free savings account
why: the right home for a goal 3 or more years away: no tax on the growth, up to R46,000 a year from 1 March 2026, opened with a bank or investment platform you can check on the FSCA register
fits: you have a cushion, no expensive debt, and a goal years away such as school fees, a deposit or extra retirement savings
not_when: you are still building the cushion or paying a mashonisa or store account; a tax-free account is for money you will not touch
setup: check the provider on the FSCA register → open the account labelled 'tax-free' → set a recurring transfer for the day after payday → keep a running total of deposits → never exceed R46,000 a year or R500,000 lifetime
walkthrough: Choose a provider: most big banks, unit trust companies and investment platforms offer a tax-free savings account; GoTyme Bank was not reported to offer one as of 2026, so ask your bank or compare a few, and check the provider's FSP number on fsca.co.za.

Ask two questions before opening: what are the fees (a tax-free fixed deposit at a bank usually has none; a unit trust charges a yearly percentage), and is the account registered as tax-free with SARS.
Open it in the app or online with your ID and tax number; it must be in your own name (a parent can open one for a child, but the child's limits are used).
Set a recurring transfer for the day after payday for the monthly number in your goal sentence; there is no legal minimum.

Keep a running total in your notes app of every deposit ever made across all your tax-free accounts: the limit is R46,000 a tax year (from 1 March 2026) and R500,000 in a lifetime, and SARS taxes anything over at 40%.
Leave it alone: withdrawals are allowed, but what you take out never gives you the contribution room back.
Never open a second tax-free account without counting the first, and never move money from the cushion into it; the cushion must stay reachable.
ten_minute_action: Open your banking app and search for 'tax-free savings'; if your bank has one, read its fee line, and if not, write down two providers to compare on fsca.co.za tomorrow.
cost: free to open at most banks; fees differ by provider (ask); annual limit R46,000 from 1 March 2026, lifetime R500,000, excess taxed at 40% by SARS (checked 2026-10-30)

name: TransUnion free annual credit report
why: TransUnion is the largest registered bureau; the National Credit Act gives you its report free once a year, and its site has a dispute page for anything wrong
fits: you want the report most lenders pull, free, and a place to dispute a wrong listing with evidence
not_when: you have never had any account, loan or contract; TransUnion may have no file on you yet, and the site may not verify you
setup: go to transunion.co.za → open the free annual credit report page → register with your own ID details → answer the verification questions or OTP → view the report → use the dispute page for wrong items
walkthrough: On your phone open transunion.co.za and find the 'free annual credit report' page (transunion.co.za/product/annual-free-credit-report); you will be asked for your South African ID number on their site, nowhere else.
Register with your details, answer the verification questions or enter the OTP sent to your phone, and the report opens on screen; it may also be emailed to you.
Read the accounts first and mark 3 things: any account you do not recognise, any account with no payment for 3 years, and anything paid that still shows as owing.
Save a screenshot or the PDF in a folder with the date; you will compare it in 3 months.

To dispute, use the 'dispute or query an item' link on TransUnion's contact page and attach your paid-up letter, statement or police case number; TransUnion must investigate free within 20 business days under section 72 of the National Credit Act.
If the site cannot verify you, phone TransUnion's call centre on 0861 482 482 and choose the option for an agent.
Never pay a 'free credit report' site that asks for a card, and diary 12 months from today for your next free report from TransUnion.
ten_minute_action: Open transunion.co.za on your phone, find the free annual credit report page, and register with your own details; mark anything on the report you do not recognise.
cost: free: one report a year under NCA section 72; TransUnion's call centre is 0861 482 482 (checked 2026-10-30)

name: uFiling (UIF online claims)
why: the Department of Employment and Labour's online portal is where an unemployment claim is lodged without a day in a queue; the same claim can be made at a labour centre if the site fails
fits: you were employed with UIF deducted, lost the job in the last 12 months, and have the UI-19 from your employer
not_when: you resigned, were never registered for UIF, or your last day was more than 12 months ago; and it needs an employment record, so it does not work for cash piece jobs
setup: get the UI-19 and salary schedule from your employer → register on ufiling.labour.gov.za → register as a work seeker → apply for unemployment benefits and upload the documents → keep signing the continuation forms
walkthrough: Get the completed UI-19 form and a salary schedule from your employer the week you leave; they must give it to you, and nothing starts without it.
Open ufiling.labour.gov.za and register with your ID number and the details on your UI-19; if the site is down, the same claim is made at your nearest labour centre.
Register as a work seeker when prompted; an unemployment claim requires it.

Choose 'Apply for benefits', then 'Unemployment benefits', and upload the UI-19, a copy of your ID, your last payslips, and the UI-2.8 banking form with your own bank account details; keep the originals.
Lodge within 12 months of your last working day; late claims are turned away.

Expect roughly 1 day of benefit for every 4 days worked, up to 365 days, at 38% to 60% of your pay (lower earners get the higher rate), paid in instalments while you submit the continuation forms the portal asks for.
If nothing happens after a few weeks, phone the UIF line on 0800 030 007 (the number published for the UIF call centre; some sources give 0800 843 843), and never pay an 'agent' to claim for you.
ten_minute_action: Message or email your employer: 'Please send me my completed UI-19 and salary schedule so I can claim UIF.' Then open ufiling.labour.gov.za and start registering.
cost: free to claim; benefits are 38% to 60% of salary, 1 day per 4 days worked up to 365 days, claim within 12 months (checked 2026-10-30)

name: XDS free credit report (Splendi)
why: XDS is the third big bureau and some lenders report only to it; its free consumer service Splendi shows the report and takes disputes online, so staggering the three bureaus gives you a free look every few months
fits: you have pulled TransUnion or Experian and want the third view, or a lender says it used XDS
not_when: you have never had any credit or contract; the bureau may have no file on you
setup: go to Splendi via xds.co.za → register with your own ID details → verify → view the report → dispute wrong items online or by phone
walkthrough: On your phone open xds.co.za and follow the link to Splendi, XDS's free consumer service; you will be asked for your South African ID number on their site only.
Register with your email and cellphone number and complete the verification they send.
Open the report and mark the same 3 things as on the other bureaus: accounts you do not recognise, accounts with no payment for 3 years, and paid accounts still showing as owing.
Screenshot or download it with the date and keep it with your TransUnion and Experian reports.
Dispute a wrong item on Splendi with your evidence attached, or phone XDS on 0860 937 000; the bureau must investigate free within 20 business days under section 72 of the National Credit Act.
If XDS does not answer within 20 business days, complain free to the NCR on 0860 627 627 or the National Financial Ombud on 0860 800 900.
Never pay a site that charges for 'your XDS report'; Splendi is free, and the National Credit Act report is free once a year anyway.
ten_minute_action: Open xds.co.za on your phone, follow the Splendi link, and register with your email and cellphone number to see your XDS report.
cost: free: Splendi is XDS's free consumer service, and the NCA guarantees one free report a year; XDS's line is 0860 937 000 (checked 2026-10-30)

name: CCMA referral
why: the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration hears unfair dismissal and severance disputes free, with no lawyer needed, and its case officers help you fill in the form
fits: you were dismissed or retrenched and the severance, notice or leave pay was not paid, or the dismissal was unfair
not_when: you were self-employed or doing cash piece jobs with no employer; the CCMA needs an employer to refer against
setup: phone 0861 16 16 16 to check the CCMA (or a bargaining council) covers you → fill in form LRA 7.11 → serve a copy on the employer → file it with the CCMA → attend the conciliation date
walkthrough: Phone the CCMA on 0861 16 16 16 and describe the dispute; they tell you whether the CCMA or a bargaining council handles it and where the nearest office is.

Note the time limit: an unfair dismissal must be referred within 30 days of the dismissal, counting weekends and holidays; a severance-only claim is referred in writing under the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, so do it in the same week.
Download form LRA 7.11 from ccma.org.za or get it at the office; the case management officers there help you complete it free.
Serve a copy on the employer (by email, fax or hand delivery with proof) and file the original with the CCMA with the proof of service.
Bring your contract, payslips, the dismissal or retrenchment letter and any messages to the conciliation; it is a meeting with a commissioner, not a court, and you may speak for yourself.
If conciliation fails, the commissioner tells you the next step (arbitration or the Labour Court); for severance, the legal minimum is 1 week's pay per completed year of service.
Never pay a 'labour consultant' who promises a win, and never sign a 'full and final' settlement at work without the amounts written on it.
ten_minute_action: Phone the CCMA on 0861 16 16 16, say what happened and when, and ask for the referral form and the time limit that applies to you.
cost: free: referring a dispute to the CCMA costs nothing, and the statutory severance minimum is 1 week's pay per completed year (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Eskom free basic electricity token
why: once your household is on the indigent register, the free units are only yours if you claim the token each month; a dial code does it in under a minute
fits: your household is registered as indigent with the municipality and Eskom supplies your prepaid electricity
not_when: you are not yet on the indigent register (apply at the municipality first), or your electricity comes from the municipality, which issues the token where you buy electricity
setup: get onto the municipal indigent register → wait for the municipality to load you on Eskom's system → dial *130*269# on the first of the month → enter the token in the meter → repeat every month
walkthrough: Apply at your municipality's indigent office first; Eskom says the municipality decides who qualifies and loads your details onto the Eskom system.
Ask the municipality when your details will be on Eskom's system; approval and loading can take a few months.
On the first of each month, dial *130*269# (Eskom's page also lists *130*869#) from the cellphone linked to your meter and follow the prompts to claim the token.
Type the 20-digit token into your prepaid meter the same way as a bought token; the free allocation is 50 kWh to 60 kWh depending on the municipality.
Claim every month; a household gets one free token a month and unused units are forfeited, they do not carry over.
If the code says you do not qualify, go back to the municipality with your indigent approval letter; Eskom cannot register you itself.
Never pay anyone offering 'free electricity tokens' for a fee; the free units come only through the municipality's register.
ten_minute_action: Check whether your household is on the municipal indigent register; if it is, dial *130*269# from the phone linked to your meter and claim this month's token.
cost: free: 50 kWh to 60 kWh of electricity a month for registered indigent households, claimed by dialling *130*269# (Eskom, checked 2026-10-30)

name: Your fund administrator's two-pot portal
why: your savings pot balance and any withdrawal live on the fund administrator's own member portal; nowhere else can show you the real number or the tax before you decide
fits: you belong to a pension, provident or retirement annuity fund and want to see your savings pot balance, or face a real emergency the cushion cannot cover
not_when: you have no retirement fund, or the need can be met from the cushion; the savings pot is the last resort, not a savings account
setup: find your fund's name on your payslip → register on the administrator's member portal → read the savings pot balance → use the tax estimate → claim only in a real emergency, once per tax year
walkthrough: Find the fund's name and your member number on your payslip or benefit statement, or ask HR; the administrator (Alexander Forbes, Old Mutual, Sanlam, Momentum, Liberty, the GEPF and others) runs the portal.
Register on the administrator's member portal or app with your ID and member number; the two-pot section shows the savings pot, the retirement pot and the vested component separately.
Read the savings pot balance; you may withdraw from this pot only, once per tax year (1 March to 28 February), with a minimum of R2,000.

Use the portal's tax estimate or the SARS two-pot calculator: the withdrawal is added to your income for the year and taxed at your marginal rate with no tax-free portion, and SARS deducts any tax you owe first.
Before claiming, ask the cushion question: would you borrow for this? If the answer is no, close the portal.

If you do claim, make sure your tax number and bank account on the portal are correct, submit, and expect the fund to request a SARS tax directive before paying; once issued, the withdrawal cannot be cancelled.
Never withdraw to pay a debt you could snowball or for a goal, and never give your portal login to anyone offering to 'claim it for you'.
ten_minute_action: Look at your payslip for your fund's name and member number, then search the administrator's member portal and register to see your savings pot balance; look, do not claim.
cost: no fee from most funds, but the withdrawal is taxed at your marginal rate; one per tax year, minimum R2,000, cannot be reversed (checked 2026-10-30)

name: Legal Aid South Africa advice line
why: free legal advice and, if you qualify on income, a free lawyer for civil matters including debt under the National Credit Act, garnishee orders and summonses; a 'Please Call Me' gets a call back
fits: you have received a summons, a garnishee is on your salary, or a lender is taking you to court and you earn under the means test
not_when: you earn more than the Legal Aid means test (R9,400 a month for a single person from April 2026), or the matter is a complaint a free ombud or regulator can handle without a lawyer
setup: phone the advice line in office hours or send a Please Call Me to 079 835 7179 → describe the matter → if you qualify, visit the nearest Justice Centre with your papers → the lawyer takes it from there
walkthrough: Phone Legal Aid South Africa's advice line between 7am and 5pm on weekdays, or send a 'Please Call Me' to 079 835 7179 and someone phones you back; it is free.
Describe the matter in plain words: a summons, a garnishee, a court date, an eviction, or a lender's threat, with the dates.

Check the means test when they ask: from April 2026 the limit for civil matters is R9,400 a month for an individual and R10,200 for a household, with a cap on movable assets; pensioners may qualify on proof of the grant.
If you qualify, go to the nearest Legal Aid Justice Centre with your ID, the court papers, the credit agreement, statements and your income proof; Legal Aid's lawyers may not ask you for payment.
Give the lawyer your owed list and your month plan; for a garnishee above 25% of basic salary, or one with no proper court order, they can apply to set it aside.
Keep every document and reply to the Justice Centre's requests quickly; a court date does not wait.
Never ignore a summons hoping it goes away, and never pay a 'legal consultant' who is not an admitted attorney.
ten_minute_action: Send a 'Please Call Me' to 079 835 7179 from your phone, and put the summons or court papers, your ID and your last payslip in one place for the call back.
cost: free if you qualify: the means test from April 2026 is R9,400 a month for an individual in civil matters (Legal Aid SA, checked 2026-10-30)

name: SASSA WhatsApp and toll-free line
why: SASSA answers payment dates, status and general grant questions by phone and on an automated WhatsApp line, which saves a day at the office for a question that takes a minute
fits: you want a payment date, an SRD status, or to know what to bring to the office before you go
not_when: you need to change banking details, apply for a permanent grant, or report a deduction; those are done at the office or on srd.sassa.gov.za, never on WhatsApp
setup: save the toll-free number 0800 60 10 11 → confirm the WhatsApp number on sassa.gov.za → message 'Hi' and follow the menu → use it for information only
walkthrough: Save SASSA's toll-free line 0800 60 10 11 in your phone; it is the number consistently published for office locations, documents and general queries.
SASSA's WhatsApp line is widely published as 082 046 8553; before you trust it, confirm the number on sassa.gov.za, because fake 'SASSA' numbers circulate on WhatsApp groups.
Message 'Hi' to the confirmed number and follow the menu for payment dates, SRD status and office information; it is automated and may answer only in office hours for anything that needs a person.
Use it for information only: never send your ID number, banking details, a card photo, a PIN or an OTP in a WhatsApp chat, even to SASSA.
For SRD applications, appeals and banking changes, use srd.sassa.gov.za; for permanent grants and deductions, go to the office with your documents.
If a WhatsApp message asks you to pay a fee, click a link, or 'confirm' your card details to release a grant, it is a scam; block it and report it at the office.
Keep the monthly payment dates SASSA announces (older persons first, then disability, then children's grants) in your notes app so your month plan starts on grant day.
ten_minute_action: Save 0800 60 10 11 in your phone as 'SASSA', then open sassa.gov.za to confirm the WhatsApp number before you message it.
cost: free: the toll-free line costs nothing and WhatsApp uses only your data (checked 2026-10-30)
